པའོ། །འཇུག་པ་ནི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཆེན་པོ་དེར་ཞུགས་པའོ། །འཕགས་པ་ནི་ལམ་དེར་འཕགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་སྦྱོང་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་འདིས་ནི་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡང་དག་ཕུལ་དུ་གྱུར་པ་དེ་སྟོན་ཏོ། །འདི་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ཡང་ཡིན་ལ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་གཞན་རྣམས་སྣང་བར་གྱུར་པ་ཡང་ཡིན་ཏེ།

teachings for the purpose of scripture, for the purpose of comprehension, and for the purpose of following the instructions. "Great Being" <note>original: Mahasattva</note> should be understood in three aspects of greatness: great armor, great engagement, and great noble ascent. In that regard, "armor" refers to making aspirations. "Engagement" refers to entering that great enlightenment. "Noble ascent" refers to this "purifying the path of the Noble Bodhisattva," which shows how they have reached the ultimate perfection. This is a "gate of Dharma" <note>original: dharmamukha</note>, and it is also the "illumination of other gates of Dharma," because through it all the meanings of the Great Vehicle appear; thus it is the illumination of the gate of Dharma. One should understand the "gate of Dharma" to be the enumeration of the Dharma. "Ultimate perfection" is so called because it transcends all phenomena and is supreme. That which is called the "presentation of the classifications" shows that the enumeration of the Dharma is to be known through worldly knowledge. That which is called "this place of knowing the presentation is inconceivable" shows that here it is the supra-mundane primordial wisdom. If one asks what is fully shown by this: it shows that by the mere presentation of the classifications of the levels, one should understand that this is not yet the actual purification of the Bodhisattva levels.

Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, having uttered merely the names of those ten levels of the Bodhisattva, sat in silence without further explaining them in detail. Then the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas, having heard merely the names of those ten levels of the Bodhisattva but not hearing the detailed classifications of the levels described, became thirsty for the teaching and thought to themselves: why is it that the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, having uttered merely the names of those ten levels of the Bodhisattva, sits in silence, letting the time pass without showing them further in detail? What is the cause and what is the condition for this? At that time, in that gathered assembly of Bodhisattvas, there sat a Bodhisattva, a Great Being named Vimukticandra <note>Moon of Liberation</note>. Then the Bodhisattva

The teaching is presented for the purpose of the scripture, to facilitate understanding, and as an instruction to be followed. One should recognize that a <term>Mahasattva</term> <gloss>Great Being</gloss> is characterized by three greatnesses: the great armor, the great engagement, and the great noble one. Regarding these, the armor refers to the making of aspirations. The engagement refers to entering into that great enlightenment. The noble one refers to the purification of the path of the noble <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>Enlightenment Being</gloss> on that path; by this, it demonstrates how one reaches the perfect excellence. 

This is both a doorway to the <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>the Buddhist Teachings</gloss> and that which causes other doorways of the <term>Dharma</term> to appear. Because all meanings of the <term>Mahayana</term> <gloss>Great Vehicle</gloss> appear, it is the illumination of the doorways of the <term>Dharma</term>. One should understand that the "doorway of the <term>Dharma</term>" refers to categories of teachings. "Perfect excellence" refers to reaching the culmination of all phenomena, thereby becoming supreme.

The phrase "by which the divisions are established" demonstrates that the categories of the <term>Dharma</term> are to be known through mundane knowledge. The phrase "the place of knowing this establishment is inconceivable" demonstrates that this refers to supramundane primordial wisdom. If one asks what is fully demonstrated by this, it shows that merely establishing the divisions of the <term>bhumi</term> <gloss>stages of awakening</gloss> should be understood as not yet being the full purification of the <term>Bodhisattva</term> stages.

###

Then, the <term>Bodhisattva</term> <term>Vajragarbha</term> <gloss>Diamond Essence</gloss> spoke only the names of those ten <term>Bodhisattva</term> stages and remained silent without explaining them further in detail. Then, the entire assembly of <term>Bodhisattvas</term>, having heard only the names of those ten <term>Bodhisattva</term> stages, became thirsty because the divisions of the stages had not been spoken. They thought to themselves: why does the <term>Bodhisattva</term> <term>Vajragarbha</term> mention only the names of these #ten stages of #the <term>Bodhisattva</term> and then remain silent, letting the time pass without showing the further divisions? What is the cause and what is the condition for this? <summary>This page explains the qualities of a Mahasattva and the distinction between mundane and supramundane knowledge of the ten bhumis. It describes the assembly's growing anticipation and confusion when Vajragarbha names the ten stages but remains silent instead of explaining them.</summary>
